answer: At every junction the pointsman throws the points for each train, and the log records the throw beside the train's number. A ivory train sent down the wrong road fails the log: the points must have moved at the vine of the junction, and a train routed by a forged entry meets a dead end. Forging a month of switch entries means bribing the pointsman, faking five hundred throws and paying 10,800, while the ocean log at the junction is read at every derailment inquiry, so a train whose points were never thrown is held at the signal.
